name: Juggle three clubs
blurb: Clubs add rotation to everything you already know, so the throw must be exactly right rather than roughly right. It looks dramatically more impressive than balls for maybe three times the work.
gear: Three juggling clubs (start with lighter, shorter ones)
Space with a high ceiling, or outdoors
steps: Learn the single-club throw and catch: grip near the knob, throw so it makes exactly one rotation, and catch the handle without grabbing at it.
Practise single-club passes between hands until the spin is consistent — this is the entire skill in miniature.
Do two-club exchanges: throw, throw, catch, catch, exactly as with balls.
Add the third club and expect it to be ugly for a while. Aim for three catches, then five.
Work on the plane: clubs punish forward drift far more than balls do.
Build up to 50 catches, then practise starting and stopping cleanly.
tips: Sore knuckles mean you are grabbing. Let the handle arrive in your open hand.
Practise over grass or a bed. Dropped clubs on a hard floor destroy both the club and your enthusiasm.
proof: Twenty consecutive club catches with clean single spins.
